recipes.name: Four-Layer Delight
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed
2 (3.4 ounce) packages instant butterscotch pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Coat a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
Beat 1/4 cup confectioners’ sugar and margarine together in a medium bowl until creamy. Mix in 1 cup pecans and flour until well combined; press into the prepared dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until very lightly browned, about 15 minutes. Cool completely.
Beat cream cheese and remaining 1 cup confectioners’ sugar together in a large bowl until well combined; fold in 1/2 of the whipped topping until incorporated. Spread over cooled crust.

Stir milk and pudding mix together in a separate bowl until well combined; allow to set up slightly. Spread over cream cheese layer; top with remaining whipped topping and sprinkle with remaining 1/8 cup pecans. Store in the refrigerator until serving time.

raw_recipe.headline: Four-Layer Delight
raw_recipe.description: This chilled four-layer delight dessert recipe has a pecan shortbread crust topped with a cream cheese layer, butterscotch pudding, and whipped topping.

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe! Instead of browning the crust, simply crush a bag of Pecan Sandies cookies and mix with a cup of melted butter to form a "crust". My mom always makes this with chocolate pudding for holidays, and there is never any left!

This recipe has been in my family for years. The 2 differences between ours and this one is: It fits perfectly into a smaller dish, an 8X11.5. A 9x13 makes layers too thin. We use a small pkg of pistachio pudding and a small pkg of French vanilla pudding. mix each pudding mix with 1 1/2 c milk and layer starting with crust, cream cheese mixture, pistachio pudding, vanilla pudding, and rest of whipped topping on top. It is the perfect spring/Easter dessert!
Definitely use the Pecan Sandies for a crust with one stick of salted butter. Bake in the oven at 300 for 10 minutes. Sprinkle chocolate chips and pecans on top for presentation. Yum!

I loved this easy dessert. I did notice that the crust did not fit in a 9 by 13 pan. So, I made it in an 8 by 8 instead. I used chocolate and butterscotch pudding. I placed the crust crumbles in individual dessert glasses and then layered the dessert on top. I garnished it with pecan halves and a hershey's kiss. They were so cute and personalized.

I make the filling with reduced-fat cream cheese, "light" whipped topping, sugar-free CHEESECAKE instant pudding and fat free evaporated milk. If I have it on hand, I'll spread another layer of light cherry pie filling over the top. I almost always have at least one person ask me for the recipe.

Made this twice. First time made exact to directions. Second time, took other reviewers suggestion and used packaged Sandies cookies with 1/2 cup melted butter for the crust ( chill it to "set up") and made with lemon pudding. Finished by sprinkling additional crushed cookies over the top. Both excellent and would not change this recipe in any other way. Both versions a huge hit.

I was looking for a "butterscotch torte" recipe that was similiar to a dessert I had at a local deli. This recipe is very close to what it was. I took the other reviewers advice too and used a package of pecan sandies for the crust. I used a stick of butter with the whole package and baked it at 350 for probably 12 minutes or so. 

Next time I will double the cream cheese layer as it didn't seem to be quite enough, and I will use a whole container of whip topping on the top.

I HAVE BEEN MAKING THIS RECIPE FOR YEARS. IT WAS GIVEN TO ME FROM MY GRANDMOTHER. I MIX IT UP WITH DIFFERENT PUDDING FLAVORS. MY FAMILY LOVES THE BANANA CREAM PIE OR COCONUT CREAM PIE VERSION. FOR THE FIRST TIME I USED THE PECAN SANDIE COOKIES, FLOUR AND BUTTER FOR THE CRUST AND IT TURNED OUT FANTASTIC!

Been making it since the 70's! Now I use real whipping cream, whipped and sweetened, because I just won't buy that artificial frozen "cream" an extra step but worth it! I also have doubled the cream cheese layer when I am making it for a crowd. Butterscotch, chocolate, pistachio pudding, each one awesome!

Only change was I used chocolate pudding. Delicious! The butterscotch flavor tastes somewhat like caramel, also delicious! Any flavor of pudding with this recipe is a no fail winner! Was not a spoonful left among 6 guests. If you don't have pecans, chopped walnuts is the next best.
Wow!!! This was a winner. I used the “SANDIES” method for the crust...no bake. And subbed Chocolate pudding for the butterscotch.
Delicious. I always add chocolate layer too. Also have done peanut butter pudding and chocolate layered. So good any way it’s made.
I ts easy and you can change the flavor of the pudding
Great tasting dessert that you can easily change flavors.
My mom has made this for years with pistachio pudding. Very good.

In the future follow the recipe exact or don't bother rating it!!!!

Been making since 70's also. I double crust and cream cheese mixture and make 2 - 8x8 pans. One without pecans and one with to please the whole family.
We make this for different occasions, but we use half chocolate half vanilla instead of butter scotch!
Love this recipe used chocolate pudding instead of butterscotch taste great!!
I've made this dessert twice, using different puddings. An easy and quick treat.
